title: China-to-Europe Trains Stop at the Border to Swap Every Wheel | China Travel Expert
description:
You picture one train rolling straight from China to Europe. It can't — the wheels don't fit the tracks.

China's railways run on 1,435 mm standard gauge. Russia, Mongolia and the rest of the former Soviet network run on 1,520 mm broad gauge. So at the border, the train stops: each carriage is lifted off its wheels and rolled onto wider bogies before it can continue. It's called a break of gauge, and it happens at crossings like Manzhouli, on the Chinese-Russian border, where the Trans-Manchurian line heads on to Moscow. Did you know the wheels change? Tell me.

🧭 Expert Tip: if you want to actually ride it, the Trans-Manchurian route (Beijing–Moscow via Manzhouli) is the one to book — you'll feel the long border stop while the bogies are swapped.

从中国到欧洲的火车,到了边境要把每节车厢的轮子都换掉——你知道吗?
